headline: Bus attack and blackouts hit Ukraine before winter

sources.title: At least 30 people killed as Russia bombs two buses in Ukraine (NBC News)
Russian bomb attack kills dozens at Ukraine bus stop (The Irish Times)
Russian missile strike on Ukraine kills 30 on packed city buses, as Moscow says "no clear path" to peace (CBS News)
Blackouts return to Kyiv as Russia prepares to freeze civilians over the winter (Euromaidan Press)

chunks.text: On October 8, 2026, a Russian glide bomb hit a bus stop in Kramatorsk, a city in eastern Ukraine near the [[front line]]. It struck two [[passenger buses]] at about 10 a.m. Ukraine's state emergency service said at least 30 people were killed and 18 were injured. President Zelenskyy warned that the [[death toll]] could {{go up}}. The regional governor {{shut down}} [[public transportation]] in Kramatorsk and a nearby city. Russia has always denied targeting [[civilians]].

verbs.wrong: To be counted a second time
verbs.why: The price of bread went up again in March. Gas prices usually go up in the summer. President Zelenskyy warned that the death toll could go up.

verbs.correct: To stop a service for a time
verbs.why: The city shut down the subway during the storm. Officials shut down the airport because of heavy snow. The regional governor shut down public transportation in Kramatorsk and a nearby city.

chunks.text: The attack came during a new [[wave]] of Russian strikes. On October 7, a [[missile]] hit an apartment building in northern Ukraine and killed 22 people. On October 8, air raid [[sirens]] {{went off}} across Kyiv as the capital {{came under}} drone attack. In late September, Ukraine's prime minister said Russia had {{kept up}} attacks on [[energy sites]] almost every day since the summer. Reports say Ukraine is also {{running low on}} [[air defense]] [[ammunition]].

verbs.wrong: To find a safe place to hide
verbs.why: The coach came under criticism after the loss. The website came under attack from hackers. On October 8, Kyiv came under drone attack.

The workers kept up their protest for three weeks. The storm kept up its heavy rain all night. Ukraine's prime minister said Russia had kept up attacks on energy sites almost every day since the summer.

verbs.wrong: To ask other countries to help
verbs.why: We are running low on milk. The hospital ran low on blood after the accident. Reports say Ukraine is running low on air defense ammunition.

chunks.text: Russian strikes also hit Ukraine's [[power grid]]. On October 8, the national [[grid operator]] ordered emergency [[power outages]] in parts of Kyiv. Strikes {{knocked out}} power in parts of four regions near the front line. City officials warned that some buildings in Kyiv could be {{cut off}} from water. The grid operator asked people to {{cut back on}} electricity on October 9, especially from 5 to 10 p.m.

verbs.wrong: To check how bad the damage is
verbs.why: The storm knocked out power to our street. Lightning knocked out the town's phone lines. Russian strikes knocked out power in parts of four regions near the front line.

verbs.correct: To stop the supply of something
verbs.wrong: To raise the price of something
verbs.why: The company cut off our gas because we did not pay the bill. Workers cut off the water while they fixed the pipe. City officials warned that some buildings in Kyiv could be cut off from water.

verbs.wrong: To pay a bill on time
verbs.why: I am trying to cut back on sugar. My doctor told me to cut back on coffee. The grid operator asked people to cut back on electricity, especially in the evening.

chunks.text: Ukrainian officials warn that this winter could be especially hard. Ukraine expects Russia to {{step up}} its [[campaign]] against the energy system as winter begins. Without power, homes can also lose heat and water. Zelenskyy said it was important for allies to deliver the [[defense packages]] they promised. He also {{called on}} President Donald Trump to increase pressure on Russia. Ukrainian [[negotiators]] were set to hold talks in the United States on October 9 and 10.

verbs.correct: To make something bigger or stronger
verbs.why: The police stepped up patrols after the robbery. The team stepped up its training before the final game. Ukraine expects Russia to step up its campaign against the energy system as winter begins.

verbs.correct: To ask someone to do something
verbs.why: The mayor called on residents to save water. The union called on the company to raise pay. Zelenskyy called on President Donald Trump to increase pressure on Russia.

mainIdea.s: A Russian bomb killed at least 30 people at a bus stop in eastern Ukraine. The attack came as strikes on the power grid caused blackouts and officials warned of a hard winter.
mainIdea.why: A glide bomb hit two passenger buses in Kramatorsk. Russian strikes also knocked out power in several regions as winter gets closer.

mainIdea.s: In eastern Ukraine, a strike on two buses left 30 people dead and closed local transit. Officials say the outages in the capital came from old equipment failing in cold weather.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the outages did not come from old equipment. Russian strikes on energy sites knocked out power and hurt the grid.

mainIdea.s: Ukraine opened a new railway line between two eastern cities this month. Officials say the trains will help families travel safely and bring heating fuel to homes before winter.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a bomb that hit two buses in Kramatorsk. It is also about Russian strikes that cut off power before winter.

tf.s: Ukraine's state emergency service said at least 30 people were killed.
tf.why: It also said 18 people were injured. Zelenskyy warned that the death toll could go up.

tf.s: The bomb struck a train station in Kramatorsk.
tf.why: It struck a bus stop and two passenger buses. Afterward, the regional governor shut down public transportation.

tf.s: Air raid sirens went off across Kyiv on October 8.
tf.why: Sirens went off across the capital as it came under drone attack.

tf.s: Ukraine's prime minister said Russia had kept up attacks on energy sites.
tf.why: In late September, he said Russia had kept up these attacks almost every day since the summer.

tf.s: Strikes knocked out power in parts of ten regions near the front line.
tf.why: Strikes knocked out power in parts of four regions near the front line.

tf.s: Zelenskyy called on President Trump to reduce pressure on Russia.
tf.why: He called on President Donald Trump to increase pressure on Russia, not reduce it.

lines.text: Did you see the news from Kramatorsk?
A Russian bomb hit a bus stop and two buses. At least 30 people were killed.
Oh no. Do they think the number will {{go up}}?
The president warned that it could. The regional governor also {{shut down}} public transportation there.
Right. He said the security situation got much worse.
What about the rest of the country?
Sirens {{went off}} across Kyiv, and the capital {{came under}} drone attack.
I read that strikes {{knocked out}} power in several regions.
Yes. Some buildings in Kyiv could even be {{cut off}} from water.
So people are being asked to {{cut back on}} electricity?
Especially in the evening. And [[keep in mind]], winter hasn't even started yet.
Officials say Russia has {{kept up}} these attacks since the summer.
And now they say it's {{stepping up}} the campaign before the cold weather.
It's [[one thing after another]] for people there.
That's how it sounds. The president also {{called on}} the United States to increase pressure on Russia.
[[Sooner or later]], those talks have to lead somewhere.

expressions.def: Used to say that problems keep coming with no break between them

expressions.def: Used to say that something will happen at some time, even if not soon
ex: Sooner or later, the price of gas will change.
